subject: Workplace Skills
title: Framing Your Message
description: A micro-lesson that makes Framing Your Message usable.

hook.text: 'We need to cut costs' triggers fear. 'We need to invest more efficiently' triggers innovation. Same situation.

buildup.text: How you frame an idea determines how people react to it. The frame shapes perception before the content is processed.

discovery.text: Frame proposals in terms of what the audience gains, not what they lose. Loss aversion makes negative framing repelling.

twist.text: The same proposal framed around the listener's priorities gets approved. Framed around yours, it gets ignored.

climax.text: Before any pitch, ask: what does this person care about? Frame your idea as the solution to their problem.

punchline.text: Frame it for their priorities. Not yours. Always.

quiz.question: How should you frame proposals to maximize influence?
options: Highlight how the proposal benefits the company overall
Frame it around what the specific audience gains and cares about
Focus on the technical merits and data
